definition: Verbal protocol analysis is a method of examining what a person says about their own mental steps during a task in order to identify the cognitive processes behind performance. In this source, it is used alongside a digit-span task to reveal behaviorally observable encoding strategies that supported unusually strong memory.

reasons: The source does not support the general methodological definition that verbal protocol analysis examines a person’s report of their own mental steps to infer cognitive processes; it only says the study used verbal protocol analysis/protocol analysis to identify behavioral indices of encoding processes in a digit-span task.

The second sentence is tied to one specific study context, but the source does not support the broader phrasing about the method’s general use or the claim that it reveals 'behaviorally observable encoding strategies' in general.

The definition claims verbal protocol analysis is “a method of examining what a person says about their own mental steps.” The packet does not describe protocol analysis in terms of collecting or analyzing a person’s verbal reports of their own mental steps.

While the packet supports that the study used “digit-span task combined with verbal protocol analysis” and that it “identify[ies] direct behavioral indices of idiosyncratic encoding processes underlying the superior memory performance,” it does not specifically support the wording that it “reveal[s] behaviorally observable encoding strategies” (the packet uses “direct behavioral indices” and “encoding processes,” without the term “strategies”).

The claim that the encoding strategies “supported unusually strong memory” is only indirectly supported; the packet states encoding processes underlie “superior memory performance,” but does not explicitly characterize them as “supporting” it in those exact terms.
